So, you want to be a better person?

Well I'll let you in on a little secret...

It is easy.

...Wait, that's it?

No, let me finish. It is easy BUT you make it difficult.

Want to be better?

Get your act together.

Start taking responsibility for yourself and quit passing blame onto everything else. Stop imagining yourself as the victim. You are solely responsible for your own happiness so take that role a little more seriously and give yourself a bit more respect and care. Others may have hurt you in the past or perhaps you have hurt yourself but regardless of what it is, you need to forgive.

Why?

You are anchoring yourself to the past, you are unable to move on, unable to progress. An external factor may have laid the anchor on you but you are the one who continues to hold onto it.

Let it go.

It does not define you. It is not you.

Your happiness is in your hands, it is literally within yourself. You are responsible for it. It is not over there, it is not over here, it is not in that material good, it is not in your significant other, it is in you. Stop making excuses, you are only doing yourself a great disservice. The sooner you let go of that which anchors you, the sooner you can take the first step towards being a better you.

Want a hint in becoming a better person?

Clean up every aspect of your life.

Stop filling yourself with junk, both material and immaterial. Stop indulging in sorrow, regret, anger, pain, jealousy, envy, fear and rewarding it with junk that only serves to perpetuate your endless cycle of sadness.

Stop yourself consuming mindless junk, stop watching mindless television, stop consuming mindless images, stop consuming mindless content.

For the love of all that is holy, clean your place up. Your immediate surroundings and the condition in which you keep it is usually just a reflection of your interior. So if it is a chaotic mess, guess how you must feel on the inside. Align the external with the internal. If you don't know where to start perhaps this is a good place. If your external matches how you'd like to be internally then you make the process much easier because you are literally surrounded by it for most of the time.

Stop making excuses and most importantly stop blaming yourself and feeding the cycle, blaming yourself is self-indulgent, accept your errors as human nature, it is something we all share in common. We all fall down every now and then but we all get back up.

As the great Chumbawamba once put most eloquently,

"I get knocked down but I get up again, you're never gonna keep me down".

You make a mistake, great!

It is an opportunity for you to learn from the experience and build a step to get closer to where you'd like to be. Be thankful for hardship and adversity. They only serve to make you a stronger person and to help strengthen your resolve. Your hardships define you but it is up to you if they serve as a stepping stone in overcoming and becoming a stronger being or if they serve as an inflated impenetrable obstacle that serves to keep you right where you are.

As the late Bruce Lee once stated,

"There are no limits. There are only plateaus, but you must not stay there, you must go beyond them".

Remove everything that only serves to anchor you.

Whether it be a toxic relationship/friendship, whether it be mindless entertainment, whether it be non-nutritional junk food, whether it be self-loathing, whether it be blame, whether it be regret, whether it be pain, whether it be fear.

Do not indulge too much in that which insulates, it creates a comfort zone. While it is a good idea to take a breather every now and then and celebrate and reward yourself, you cannot stay there forever. Otherwise you have halted your progression.

American author J. A. Shedd once wrote,

"A ship in harbor is safe, but that is not what ships are made for."

Do not be afraid. You will fall, it is inevitable but it is up to you how long you stay down there. That which doesn't kill you only serves to make you stronger. I've always believed that we are defined more by our failures than by our successes.

Nelson Mandela once stated,

"I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it. The brave man is not he who does not feel afraid, but he who conquers that fear."

Those that ridicule and hate are only doing so in order to offload the pain that they're experiencing inside, it brings momentary satisfaction that is as fleeting as they're compassion for others. Do not hate these people, for they are suffering the most, the more hate they unload, the more they are surrounded by fear. Only feel sympathy for their struggle and for them and move on. Whatever they may hurl at you is not something that defines you, it is something that defines them.

Your reality is in your own hands, you create your own reality. Whether you create one of happiness and joy or unconsciously create one of sadness and fear. Regardless, it takes effort and if you're not willing to expend, then you will remain.

In summary,

  • Realise and internalise that you are solely responsible for your own happiness.
  • Recognise the problem that hinders your progression and recognise it as a problem. You have successfully separated yourself from it
  • Forgive whatever it is that is anchoring you. The third and frankly most important step towards bettering yourself.
  • Put an end to self-indulgence and blame, it only perpetuates the cycle of sorrow.
  • Clean and organise yourself and your surroundings, throw out that which holds you back. Whatever it may be. No more junk for the mind, body and spirit.
  • Realise that by reading this and following these steps you are already in the process of bettering yourself, so why stop now?

Bettering yourself should not feel like a chore, it may in the beginning as you start to detach yourself from the bubbling bog that you may currently inhabit but in doing so, you are literally taking steps towards your own happiness, so why can't every step be fraught with increasing joy and celebration?

Don't be so hard on yourself.

Enjoy the journey, for each one is unique for every individual, what will you discover on yours?

It is all up to you.

You can do it, have faith. Do not have hope. Hope create a false sense of security, when you hope you are expecting something from the external to create change. Have faith that the change will come from within you and nowhere else. Believe you can make a difference because ultimately, you are capable of doing so.

You are at the steering wheel of your ship called life.
